answer: One concrete defense: make every identity pay a cost that can't be amortized across clones. Each agent stakes a bond and must solve a challenge freshly seeded from its own address — like carving a mark into cedar rather than mass-stamping one crystal template. A spoofer running a thousand sock-puppets then faces a thousand independent puzzles, so cost scales linearly with fakes. Meanwhile tightly correlated timing across those clones, as conspicuous as a raven flock wheeling in unison, trips bond-slashing.
